channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Caiado critica juros e diz que governo ‘enrolou a população’ antes do Desenrola
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized the Selic rate of 14.75% and accused the federal government of having 'misled the population' by encouraging consumption, production, and loans before launching the Desenrola debt renegotiation program. He questioned the logic of releasing savings to pay what he called 'loan-shark' interest rates, calling for clearer economic policies. The Desenrola 2.0 program has renegotiated R$20 billion in family debts, with 1.4 million agreements and an average discount of 85%, reducing the total owed to R$2.7 billion.

item.title: Moraes rejeita pedido de adiamento e mantém julgamento de Eduardo Bolsonaro nesta terça
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied a request from the Public Defender's Office to postpone the trial of Eduardo Bolsonaro, keeping it scheduled for this Tuesday in the First Chamber. Eduardo Bolsonaro, the former federal deputy and son of ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, is accused of obstructing justice by attempting to impede the investigation into the January 8 coup plot, including seeking U.S. sanctions against Brazilian officials. The charge carries a penalty of 1 to 4 years in prison, with possible increases due to aggravating circumstances.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro sugere 'rompimento geral' com Novo após Zema criticar Flávio por relação com Vorcaro
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro suggested a 'complete break' with the Novo party after pre-candidate Romeu Zema criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for his relationship with banker Daniel Vorcaro, linked to the financing of the film 'Dark Horse'. Zema defended that Vorcaro's 2022 donation to Novo occurred without suspicion at the time and argued he should have donated more. The rift between Zema and Flávio Bolsonaro intensified after revelations of funding requests to Vorcaro for the Bolsonaro film, which Zema called 'imperdoável'.

item.title: Lula chega à França para reunião do G7; governo vê chance de reunião com Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva arrived in France to attend the G7 summit as a guest, with the Brazilian government assessing the possibility of an informal bilateral meeting with Donald Trump during the event, despite no prior scheduling. If the meeting occurs, it could address potential U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods (up to 37.5%), rare earths, organized crime, and trade. Lula also has confirmed bilateral meetings with Emmanuel Macron, Interpol Secretary-General Valdecy Urquiza, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi.

item.title: Lula sanciona novo Marco Legal do Transporte Público; veja principais pontos
item.description: President Lula sanctioned the new Legal Framework for Public Collective Transportation, with vetoes, establishing a national policy that separates company remuneration from passenger numbers, encouraging payment by kilometers traveled to reduce overcrowding and improve service in remote areas. The law also increases transparency, sets targets for punctuality, safety and accessibility, and promotes less polluting technologies, taking effect in one year.

item.title: Lula embarca para participar do G7 sem agenda com Trump e deve reforçar crítica ao tarifaço americano
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva traveled to France to attend the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, where he plans to criticize the potential U.S. imposition of 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods under Section 301. No formal meeting with Trump is scheduled, but an informal conversation on the sidelines remains possible. The Brazilian government views the tariff proposal as the only U.S. measure likely to be revised in the short term, currently under discussion by a working group established after Lula and Trump’s May 7 meeting.

item.title: Primeira turma do STF deve dar recados sobre EUA em julgamento que pode condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: The First Chamber of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) is expected to use the trial of Eduardo Bolsonaro — accused of coordinating sanctions against Brazilian authorities with the Trump administration — to send messages against foreign interference in the Judiciary. The same chamber that sentenced Jair Bolsonaro to 27 years in prison previously emphasized judicial independence and denounced efforts to coerce the Court by foreign powers. The current trial unfolds amid renewed U.S.-Brazil tensions and as prosecutors consider expanding the investigation to include Senator Flávio Bolsonaro over allegations tied to the financing of the film 'Dark Horse'.

item.title: Desejo acima da renda: preocupado com a popularidade, Planalto mapeia ‘consumo aspiracional’
item.description: The Lula government is mapping 'aspirational consumption' as a strategy to bridge the gap between objective economic improvements (GDP growth, low unemployment, real income rise, controlled inflation) and the public’s negative perception of his administration. The initiative seeks to align government communication with citizens’ symbolic desires and status aspirations, going beyond mere economic indicators, to recover popularity ahead of the 2026 elections. The subscriber-only article highlights internal concern over the disconnect between macroeconomic data and popular sentiment.

item.title: Relação com Vorcaro, delação e celular: as desconfianças que assombram a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is facing internal distrust linked to his alleged ties with Vorcaro, claims of plea bargain cooperation, and the use of a controversial cellphone — issues compounding declining poll numbers and undermining campaign cohesion. The exclusive article highlights how these concerns are eroding trust among allies and troubling his team, though full access requires a subscription.

item.title: Campanha do Brasil na Copa do Mundo dificilmente terá reflexos na política
item.description: The analysis argues that Brazil's victories or defeats in the FIFA World Cup have no significant impact on electoral outcomes, debunking the belief that football success favors the government at the polls. The argument is based on historical data from previous World Cups, which show no consistent correlation between the team's performance and political results.

item.title: El Niño deve ‘queimar’ reserva de hidrelétricas e encarecer tarifas de energia em 2027
item.description: NOAA confirmed the official onset of El Niño with a 63% probability of reaching 'very strong' status between November 2026 and January 2027, potentially placing it among the most intense since 1950. While the immediate impact is not severe, the phenomenon threatens to deplete Brazil’s hydroelectric reserves, which could drive up energy tariffs in 2027 and raise concerns among experts.

item.title: Lula deve se encontrar com primeira-ministra do Japão e discutir acordo com Mercosul
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is set to meet with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on the sidelines of the G7 summit next week to discuss initiating negotiations for a trade agreement between Japan and Mercosur.

item.title: Brasileiro Poatan perde a luta principal do UFC Casa Branca
item.description: Brazilian fighter Alex Poatan was knocked out by French contender Ciryl Gane at the UFC White House event held on the South Lawn of the presidential residence in Washington D.C., preventing him from becoming the first fighter to win titles in three weight classes. Poatan stated he has no regrets about moving up to heavyweight and will decide with his team whether to stay in the division or return to light heavyweight. The event took place on the same day as President Donald Trump's 80th birthday.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: imagem negativa de Trump entre brasileiros sobe seis pontos em um mês e vai a 45%
item.description: Negative perceptions of Donald Trump among Brazilians rose from 39% to 45% in one month, according to Genial/Quaest, driven by the designation of criminal groups as terrorists and a proposed new tariff against Brazil. The increase was strongest among non-Lulist left-wing voters (from 66% to 84%), while Bolsonarists saw a three-point rise to 15%. Despite this, 46% of Brazilians believe Lula should maintain an allied relationship with Trump.

item.title: França sedia cúpula do G7 dominada por Trump e conflito com o Irã
item.description: France hosts the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, focusing on the US-Iran agreement to end the war, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, AI regulation, and transatlantic tensions. Donald Trump arrives after celebrating his 80th birthday, while Macron pushes for global economic balance and tech oversight. Anti-G7 protesters clashed with police in Geneva, and leaders from Brazil, Egypt, India, Kenya, and South Korea are expected as guests.

item.title: Gilmar elogia FHC e chama Plano Real de maior programa social do país
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes praised former President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and called the Plano Real the largest social program ever implemented in Brazil, emphasizing its monetary stabilization and protection of low-income populations. He shared an article by former Finance Minister Pedro Malan, highlighting how the plan combined political will and institutional capacity to overcome hyperinflation and rebuild the country’s economic foundations. Malan warned that structural challenges such as low growth and inequality persist today and suggested that commitments to fiscal responsibility and inflation control should be reaffirmed in 2026.

item.title: A eleição e a licença para gastar
item.description: The drop in diesel and gasoline prices in May, according to the IPCA, might be seen as evidence of success for the government’s tax cuts and fuel subsidies under President Lula. However, the article questions whether this price reduction actually translates into electoral support, especially since the full content is behind a paywall. It invites scrutiny of the link between low fuel costs and voter sentiment.

item.title: Apoio à candidatura de Flávio já sai caro a seus mantenedores
item.description: The article questions the political and financial backing of Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 candidacy, suggesting supporters may be taking significant risks if he loses or proves ineffective. It raises the possibility of a revanchist government modeled after Trump 2.0, warning of potential strategic concessions — such as the Amazon or Petrobras — in exchange for foreign support, particularly from the United States.

item.title: Gilberto Gil defende “união” contra “ascensão da direita” no Brasil
item.description: Singer and former Minister of Culture Gilberto Gil urged political unity to counter polarization and the rise of the right in Brazil, in an interview with the Financial Times. He stated that the left better understands its purpose and is more invested in national progress and Brazil’s future. Gil noted his ongoing meetings with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to discuss their respective political commitments.

item.title: Lula tenta tirar verde e amarelo do bolsonarismo sob impulso de Copa, LGBTs e moda
item.description: President Lula is leading a PT campaign to redefine national symbols, attempting to dissociate green and yellow from Bolsonarism by leveraging the World Cup, LGBTQ+ support, and fashion as vehicles of national sovereignty. The move comes amid uncertainty in the Brazilian national team, which is competing in the World Cup without a fixed visual identity and with a variable lineup, causing doubts for coach Carlo Ancelotti.

item.title: Presidente eleito em outubro poderá indicar um quinto dos ministros do STF e tribunais superiores
item.description: The president elected in October 2026 will be able to appoint up to one-fifth of the ministers in the superior courts, with particular impact on the STF, where they could name 36% of the justices. These appointments do not require adherence to pre-prepared lists by the Judiciary, granting the Executive greater autonomy in selecting magistrates. The potential influence over the Court’s composition has sparked debate about judicial independence and the balance of powers.

item.title: Do texto de Nelson sobre vira-latas ao editorial “pit bull” de O Globo
item.description: The text examines Nelson Rodrigues' 1958 expression 'complexo de vira-latas' as a critique of Brazilians' self-perceived inferiority on the global stage, particularly in sports and politics, and its revival by Lula to describe the Bolsonaro family's alleged subservience to the United States. It links this concept to historical editorials in 'O Globo,' such as the June 14, 1964 piece anticipating national 'bankruptcy,' revealing a recurring pattern of national self-doubt during periods of political and economic crisis.

item.title: Por que Michelle e Tarcísio ainda não entraram na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is struggling due to the lack of support from key figures in the Bolsonarist right, such as Michelle Bolsonaro and Tarcísio de Freitas. Michelle feels disrespected and hurt for not being consulted before his presidential bid and for being passed over as a potential running mate, while Tarcísio is focusing on his re-election in São Paulo and avoiding nationalizing his campaign, leaving Flávio without the necessary structural backing.

item.title: Romário é acusado de praticar “machismo estrutural” ao comentar jogo
item.description: Senator Romário (PL-RJ) was accused by federal deputy Fernanda Melchionna (Psol-RS) of practicing 'structural machismo' after stating that journalist Fernanda Gentil 'does not know much about football' during commentary on the Brazil-Morocco draw in the 2026 World Cup. Romário defended his remark, claiming that viewing the draw as negative stemmed from a lack of football knowledge, and praised Morocco’s technical performance. Gentil responded on Instagram with a photo alongside Romário and Bebeto, writing she had 'never been in better company'.

item.title: Como o populismo bolsonarista incentiva o populismo lulista
item.description: The text argues that the strong populist right-wing opposition (bolsonarist) is pushing the Lula government, despite its Workers’ Party roots, to adopt more populist and immediate measures — such as elevated public spending and distributive laws — to retain electoral support, creating a bidding war of benefits that undermines fiscal balance and the quality of public policy.

item.title: Lula sanciona com vetos novo marco legal do transporte coletivo
item.description: President Lula signed into law the new Legal Framework for Public Collective Transportation, with vetoes, establishing national parameters for financing, management, and service quality. The law diversifies funding sources beyond fares, introduces performance- and distance-based payment for operators, and mandates transparency, minimum quality standards, and incentives for sustainable transit.

item.title: Lula sanciona com vetos novo marco do transporte público
item.description: President Lula signed into law the new urban public transport framework with vetoes, amending the City Statute and the National Urban Mobility Policy. The vetoes removed mandatory full funding of free fares by states and municipalities, tied subsidies to operator remuneration, and other provisions that could create permanent expenditures, aiming to uphold fiscal responsibility and preserve subnational autonomy.

item.title: PL marca data para lançar candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Liberal Party (PL) announced it will hold a national convention on July 25 in São Paulo to formally launch Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign. The choice of São Paulo breaks from the party’s recent tradition of launching Jair Bolsonaro’s candidacies in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Protesto anti-G7 em Genebra tem carro queimado e termina em confronto
item.description: Anti-G7 protests in Geneva, Switzerland, turned violent, with a Tesla vehicle set on fire and clashes between demonstrators and police using rubber bullets and water cannons. The protests occurred a day before the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France, 45 km away, echoing similar unrest in 2003 when Lula attended his first G8 summit as a guest.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei do Marco Legal do Transporte Público Coletivo
item.description: President Lula signed Law No. 15.432/2026, establishing the Legal Framework for Collective Public Transport, aiming to modernize financing and regulation of urban transport through diversified funding sources such as advertising, commercial exploitation, and the Cide Combustíveis tax. The law reduces reliance on user fares, promotes fare and physical integration, transparency, renewable energy transition, and sets minimum quality standards with operator remuneration tied to performance. Presidential vetoes were applied to preserve fiscal sustainability and avoid overburdening existing free or discounted fare policies.

item.title: Lula embarca rumo à França para participar da cúpula do G7
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has departed for France to attend the G7 summit in Évian, where he will represent Brazil for the tenth time. His agenda includes discussions on the global economy, sustainable development, and regulation of big techs, with potential informal talks expected with U.S. President Donald Trump amid trade tariff tensions. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin will assume presidential duties during Lula's absence.

item.title: Gol da Alemanha: novo 7 a 1 faz Brasil perder artilharia de todas as Copas
item.description: Germany defeated Curaçao 7-1 in their 2026 World Cup opener, surpassing Brazil in all-time World Cup goal tally with 239 goals to Brazil's 238. Brazil will have a chance to reclaim the top spot when they face Haiti in their second group C match on Friday. The article contrasts this result with Brazil's infamous 7-1 loss to Germany in the 2014 World Cup semifinals.

item.title: Lula vai à França para reuniões do G7 e tentará novo encontro com Trump
item.description: President Lula is in France to attend the G7 meetings and seeks a bilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump to discuss new trade tariffs imposed on Brazil. While official G7 activities begin on Tuesday, Lula arrived early to pursue a meeting with Trump, who only attends the opening session on Monday.

item.title: PL lança Flávio Bolsonaro à Presidência em SP no final de julho
item.description: The Liberal Party has set São Paulo as the venue for its national convention in late July to officially nominate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro as its presidential candidate, citing his support from Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and Mayor Ricardo Nunes, along with the state’s electoral weight. This decision contrasts with Jair Bolsonaro’s previous conventions in Rio de Janeiro, where the bolsonarist base has weakened due to legal setbacks, the cassation of Claudio Castro, and the rise of Lula-aligned Eduardo Paes. Flávio Bolsonaro was nominated in December by his incarcerated father to run in his stead.

item.title: PSD desobriga candidatos a governos de agendas ao lado de Caiado
item.description: The PSD will allow its gubernatorial candidates to disregard the presence of the party's presidential candidate, Ronaldo Caiado, in state-level agendas if they deem it more appropriate. This was confirmed by national party president Gilberto Kassab, who stated that candidate autonomy has been clear since the outset. While the PSD will run Caiado's campaign nationally, it grants flexibility for local adjustments.

item.title: Flávio perde força entre evangélicos, jovens e mulheres
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro lost support among evangelicals, young people, and women, as well as in the Southeast, Central-West, and North regions, allowing Lula to open a 6-point lead in the Quaest poll's second-round simulation (44% to 38%). The largest decline occurred in the Central-West/North aggregate, where Flávio's lead dropped from 14 to 2 points, and in the Southeast, where he led by 12 points in April but now holds only a 2-point edge — both within the margin of error, resulting in a technical tie. The survey, conducted June 5–8, 2026, with 2,004 respondents aged 16+, has a national margin of error of 2 percentage points and was funded by Banco Genial.

item.title: Visuais do público expressam identidade e pluralidade no Metrópoles Fashion & Design
item.description: The Metrópoles Fashion & Design 2026 showcased Brasília’s creative energy and diversity, as attendees expressed identity through fashion choices blending contemporary tailoring, streetwear, denim, and bold color contrasts against neutral bases. The event affirmed the city as a hub for authentic and circular fashion, driven by local entrepreneurs and trends emphasizing comfort, elegance, and personal expression.

item.title: Polícia investiga agressão a idoso em Copacabana por suposta motivação política
item.description: Rio de Janeiro's Civil Police are investigating an assault on Mauro Figueiredo Rocha, a 69-year-old PT militant, in Copacabana, allegedly motivated by political bias. The victim stated he was attacked by three individuals after being identified by a Benedita da Silva (PT) sticker, hearing slogans like 'it's Bolsonaro' and 'you fucking petista'. The incident drew condemnation from the PT's congressional bloc, which labeled the violence an assault on democratic values.

item.title: Renan Santos vence Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro em jogo do Brasil
item.description: Renan Santos of Missão was the only one among six pre-candidates to correctly predict the score of Brazil's 2026 World Cup opener, forecasting a 1–1 draw against Morocco. All others — Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Aécio Neves (PSDB), and Romeu Zema (Novo) — predicted a Brazilian victory. The G1 consulted pre-candidates who had at least 2% in voting intentions in the Quaest poll of June 10.

item.title: O país dividido também no comparecimento eleitoral
item.description: Compulsory voting in Brazil may function more as a bureaucratic class filter than as a tool for democratic inclusion, according to Jairo Nicolau in his book 'O País Dividido: Two Decades of Presidential Elections in Brazil'. The author argues that electoral turnout reflects structural inequalities, where socially vulnerable groups face barriers to voting despite the legal obligation. This challenges the common narrative that compulsory voting strengthens democracy in the country.

item.title: Cresce apelo no PSD para que Kassab seja vice de Caiado na disputa ao Planalto
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, national president of the PSD, is gaining strength as a potential vice-presidential candidate on Ronaldo Caiado’s ticket for the 2026 elections. Although he notes another name could still be chosen, party allies already view him as the best figure to unite the PSD behind Caiado’s project. Kassab publicly stated he is available to join the ticket, thanking the support of Jorge Bornhausen and Heráclito Fortes.

item.title: Flávio avança na pré-campanha sob pressão de casos no STF envolvendo Dark Horse, Lula e Vorcaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro advances in his 2026 presidential pre-campaign but faces multiple STF and PF investigations tied to the financing of the film Dark Horse by Daniel Vorcaro, including allegations of illicit cash and abuse of economic power. He is also under investigation for alleged slander against President Lula and is being sought for inclusion in the probe into Eduardo Bolsonaro’s activities in the U.S. These fronts challenge his image as a moderate Bolsonarist and risk his eligibility if convicted.

item.title: Câmara corre para aprovar redução da maioridade penal, enquanto PEC da Segurança Pública está parada
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is moving to approve reducing the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16, while the Public Security PEC, approved in March, remains stalled in the Senate due to lack of interest from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre in advancing it, undermining Lula’s electoral agenda. The opposition is leveraging the criminal responsibility issue to boost its campaign, revealing a legislative agenda misalignment driven by electoral interests, despite earlier attempts to include the topic in the Security PEC being withdrawn to ease approval with left-wing party support.

item.title: O delicado acervo do novo ministro do TCU para o governo Lula
item.description: The new TCU minister, Odair Cunha, inherited a docket of 7,306 cases, including two with significant implications for the Lula government: the R$12 million transfer to Rio’s samba schools, notably R$1 million to Acadêmicos de Niterói for a 2026 samba-enredo celebrating Lula, and the ongoing audit of federal government corporate cards, which totaled R$55.5 million in presidential spending from 2023 to 2025. While the first case sparks political debate due to its symbolic association with the president, the second highlights a long-standing lack of transparency, with 92% of the Vice-Presidency’s expenses classified as secret and the TCU historically pushing for detailed, immediate disclosure of non-secret expenditures.

item.title: Bolsonaro toca até pandeiro em IA de Flávio, e petistas estudam acionar TSE
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro posted an AI-generated video showing his father, Jair Bolsonaro, playing the pandeiro and dancing in favela settings with the message 'Pix is Bolsonaro's, my love', in reaction to Lula's protest sign stating 'Pix is Brazil's'. Despite Jair Bolsonaro being barred by the STF from using social media directly or through intermediaries due to his conviction for attempted coup, the video was shared by Flávio, raising concerns about electoral law violations, with PT supporters considering legal action before the TSE.

item.title: Ação popular quer barrar uso da AGU para defesa de Alexandre de Moraes
item.description: A popular action filed in the Federal Court of Brasília seeks to block the use of the Advocacy-General of the Union (AGU) to defend Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes in a lawsuit brought by Rumble and Trump Media, who accuse him of censorship and arbitrary arrests of Bolsonaro supporters. The action challenges the legality of the AGU’s involvement in defending a STF minister, arguing it undermines judicial independence and national sovereignty, while the Brazilian government maintains it is a matter of functional immunity.

item.title: Um Partido Liberal contra a liberdade
item.description: The text critiques the ideological inconsistency of Brazilian politicians, highlighting the gap between rhetoric and action. The Lula government is cited as an example for promoting the Desenrola program twice as a solution to Brazilians' debt, yet with outcomes that contradict its liberal or financially emancipatory discourse. The author suggests that parties claiming to be liberal often act against individual liberty when their institutional or electoral interests are at stake.

item.title: Com caso Master e novo tarifaço, Flávio Bolsonaro perde apoio entre evangélicos, mulheres e jovens, aponta pesquisa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro lost support among evangelicals, women, youth, and in the Southeast region due to his involvement with Daniel Vorcaro in financing a film about Jair Bolsonaro and the new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products, according to Genial/Quaest poll. 65% of respondents said he erred in seeking financing, 62% associate him with corruption, and Lula now leads by six points in a hypothetical runoff (44% to 38%). The PL candidate lost his lead among voters aged 16–34, where he previously led, and saw his Southeast advantage vanish, dropping from a 12-point lead to a technical tie.

item.title: Nikolas cita Janja ao negar uso de verba pública na Copa
item.description: Federal Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) denied using public funds for his trip to the United States to watch Brazil's World Cup 2026 opener, stating he paid with his own money. In an Instagram story, he joked that people were confusing him with First Lady Janja Lula da Silva, insisting his name is Nikolas Ferreira, not Janja. During his visit to MetLife Stadium, he praised a fan wearing a 'Lula thief' jersey and linked Morocco's team to the PT based on the flag's colors and the match date (the 13th).

item.title: A última medida eleitoreira de Lula antes da campanha eleitoral começar
item.description: President Lula launched a credit package of R$ 5 to 7 billion for motorcycle financing targeting delivery workers and app-based motorcyclists, backed by the FGO, with up to 48-month terms and possible manufacturer discounts. The initiative, named Move Brasil – Entregadores e Moto Apps, aims to support workers who rely on motorcycles for income. Government aides suggest this may be the last major electoral measure before the 2026 campaign begins.
